correctness.rationale: For any conjugate-linear A on a complex two-space and |q|=r<=1, reconstruct B=M*, its symmetric Takagi diagonal form diag(a,b), a>=b>=0, and skew coefficient kappa. With alpha=(1+r)/2, beta=(1-r)/2, tau=sqrt(1-r^2), h=alpha*a-beta*b, v=alpha*a+beta*b, c=tau*kappa, constrained bilinear values after a freely rotating determinant phase equal a convex combination of points on two centered nested ellipses minus c. The segment-union lemma fills the larger ellipse, including line/point degeneracies, so continuous radial moduli cover exactly [dist(c,E),maxdist(c,E)]. For real kappa, maximizing v^2+d^2-(v^2-h^2)cos^2(theta)-2dh cos(theta) gives the asserted dh=Delta transition; minimum equals (d-h)+. Independently recomputed the bilinear formula, overlap and ellipse containment for 200 complex random orthonormal bases and parameters, without using the submitted checker. These are finite diagnostics only; universality is supplied by the algebraic ellipse proof.
